body_markdown:
*DUB6* writes:


Sajeev,


Hagerty ran an article about[using GPS trackers](https://www.hagerty.com/media/advice/gps-trackers-the-last-line-of-theft-defense/) as a defense against auto theft. My question deals with the defenses of where you store your classic cars. (And often other valuable objects such as tools and automobilia.)


I have a “shut the barn door after the horse is gone” interest in this, because recently my shop was broken into and I lost many valuables. Insurance will address many things, but a few of the items are virtually irreplaceable to me (mostly nostalgic).


I’m interested in your view and your readers’ input on what systems, installs, alarms, etc. they use.


*Sajeev* answers:


I, too, look forward to everyone’s comments, because this is not a one-size-fits-all solution. But first, an admission:


Most of the stuff with nostalgic value in my collection is worth scrap value to most folks. And it’s within my single-family home, covered by its security system.


[Sajeev Mehta](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/sajeev-mehta/)


Many of the Mehta family’s vintage cars live in a third-party storage facility, and they aren’t exactly the bells of the ball. Case in point: I heard one person refer to[my beloved Mercury Montego MX Brougham](https://www.hagerty.com/media/hagerty-community/our-two-cents-the-first-car-we-rode-in/#:~:text=substitute.%E2%80%9D%20%E2%80%93%20Eddy%20Eckart-,1975%20Mercury%20Montego%20MX,-Sajeev%20Mehta%20(Actually) as “The Banana Car.”


Allow me to throw out a few notions to get the comments section eager to share their own conclusions.


1. A monitored security/fire system is a good start, but this feels more useful in densely populated areas where houses have attached garages.
2. There are a host of unmonitored camera systems available for a three-figure price tag, either with the (currently controversial) cloud form of storage, or closed circuit cameras with SD cards or external hard drives.
3. A car is much harder to steal if it’s missing a fuel-pump fuse, or has a steering wheel lock with the wheel turned (to make towing difficult).
4. Commonly stolen car parts,[like tailgates](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=a1669c2d6fe4ecbb&rlz=1C5GCCM_en&sxsrf=AKL5yDizb4mpfUUuzsKZOeMJWkFRwH7Dmg:1793287573199&udm=28&fbs=ACAhTvwdifjn2dKXmjtOfBxVFl_kNo0J7LRbgf5U9cgi9kOJRhZo2b70ls_k56Dkh0A5OtKMTwKvdYqlPsNftR_Np72-QCH39A5ekrA_kemM8wdUuqDKfBK0M9lGma6k5bCLOBrup502bqtTn4HB74GGZrQybX_6Z9Pv8xuB7fmHsq_PvioUNt_-j9-TQMC7dmwZTyQYjHnhyyk8cwYVUWTkLhvM6AYoAA&q=truck+tailgate+anti+theft&ved=1t:220175&ictx=111&biw=1157&bih=575&dpr=2&safe=active&ssui=on) , have anti-theft measures available in the aftermarket. (I have a worm-gear clamp glued to my tailgate hinge, because I am super cheap.)
5. Apple allows about 30 AirTags per account, managed with the[Find My](https://www.apple.com/icloud/find-my/) app. I assume Google Android’s max count is[similar](https://www.google.com/android/find/) .


1. If you need more, consider[asset tracking tools](https://www.google.com/search?q=small+business+asset+tracking&sca_esv=837d3543a571deb7&rlz=1C5GCCM_en&biw=1157&bih=575&sxsrf=AKL5yDhNaZRlmODUxSszkLGcPMASpA7Ueg%3A1793220462228&ei=bl_iau6-Dc-3qtsPm5uY6Qs&uact=5&oq=small+business+asset+tracking&gs_lp=Egxnd3Mtd2l6LXNlcnAiHXNtYWxsIGJ1c2luZXNzIGFzc2V0IHRyYWNraW5nMgQQABgeMgQQABgeMgYQABgIGB4yBhAAGAgYHjILEAAYgAQYigUYhgMyCBAAGIkFGKIEMggQABiJBRiiBEj2BFC8Ali8AnACeAGQAQCYAc8BoAHPAaoBAzItMbgBA8gBAPgBAZgCA6ACkwLCAgoQABhHGNYEGLADmAMAiAYBkAYIkgcFMi4wLjGgB-0EsgcDMi0xuAfsAcIHBTItMS4yyAcXgAgB&sclient=gws-wiz-serp&safe=active&ssui=on) used by small businesses.


6. Security doesn’t necessarily need to be expensive, as it can be free if you love dogs and get the correct breed for sentry tasks. (Creative accounting isn’t just for big companies!)


For the sake of civility in the comments section, I am purposefully avoiding the element of personal defense. We already know our needs in that regard, so I look forward to reading everyone’s thoughts below!
